article.title: EU's Top Court Upholds Record €4.1 Billion Google Android Antitrust Fine, Rejecting Google's Final Appeal
article.summary: Europe's Court of Justice dismissed Google and Alphabet's appeal on July 2, 2026, confirming a roughly €4.1 billion penalty over Android licensing practices and leaving no further right to appeal.
article.body_markdown:
## Overview

Europe's top court has upheld a roughly €4.1 billion ($4.7 billion) antitrust fine against Google and its parent company Alphabet over the way the company licenses its Android operating system, according to [Tech Xplore](https://techxplore.com/news/2026-07-eu-court-bn-euro-google-1.html). The Court of Justice of the European Union dismissed Google's appeal on July 2, 2026, according to [BleepingComputer](https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/legal/google-loses-final-appeal-to-overturn-41-billion-eu-fine/), in a decision that leaves the company with no further right to appeal, according to [Tech Xplore](https://techxplore.com/news/2026-07-eu-court-bn-euro-google-1.html).

In its ruling, the court stated that "The appeal brought by Google and its parent company Alphabet against the judgment of the General Court is dismissed," according to [Engadget](https://www.engadget.com/2206550/google-loses-final-appeal-over-eu-antitrust-fine/).

## What We Know

The European Commission first imposed the penalty in 2018, originally setting it at €4.34 billion, after finding that Google had abused Android's market dominance, according to [Engadget](https://www.engadget.com/2206550/google-loses-final-appeal-over-eu-antitrust-fine/). The Commission objected to three sets of restrictions: requiring device makers to pre-install Google Search and Chrome in order to license the Play Store; barring manufacturers from selling devices that ran versions of Android not approved by Google, known as anti-fragmentation agreements; and revenue-sharing agreements tied to the exclusive pre-installation of Google Search, according to [BleepingComputer](https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/legal/google-loses-final-appeal-to-overturn-41-billion-eu-fine/).

The Commission concluded that Google leveraged an Android market share of more than 80% to lock competitors out of the search market, according to [Engadget](https://www.engadget.com/2206550/google-loses-final-appeal-over-eu-antitrust-fine/).

The case has moved through the EU courts since the penalty was announced. In 2022, the EU's General Court upheld most of the Commission's findings but reduced the fine to €4.125 billion, according to [BleepingComputer](https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/legal/google-loses-final-appeal-to-overturn-41-billion-eu-fine/). Google then appealed that decision to the Court of Justice, the bloc's highest court; with the appeal now rejected, the reduced fine stands, according to [Tech Xplore](https://techxplore.com/news/2026-07-eu-court-bn-euro-google-1.html).

The Court of Justice found that the General Court "did not err in law when assessing the anticompetitive effects of the pre-installation conditions laid down by the Android agreements," according to [Engadget](https://www.engadget.com/2206550/google-loses-final-appeal-over-eu-antitrust-fine/).

## What Google Said

A Google spokesperson said the ruling "fails to recognize our significant investment to ensure Android remains open, interoperable and free," according to [BleepingComputer](https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/legal/google-loses-final-appeal-to-overturn-41-billion-eu-fine/). The company said it had already adapted its agreements to comply with the original 2018 decision, according to [BleepingComputer](https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/legal/google-loses-final-appeal-to-overturn-41-billion-eu-fine/).

The consumer group BEUC welcomed the decision as "a big win for Europe," according to [Tech Xplore](https://techxplore.com/news/2026-07-eu-court-bn-euro-google-1.html).

## Wider Context

The Android penalty is among the largest antitrust fines the EU has imposed on a technology company, according to [Tech Xplore](https://techxplore.com/news/2026-07-eu-court-bn-euro-google-1.html). It is not the company's only recent clash with Brussels: in September 2025, the Commission separately fined Google €2.95 billion for favoring its own advertising services, according to [Tech Xplore](https://techxplore.com/news/2026-07-eu-court-bn-euro-google-1.html). Google also lost an appeal over a €2.4 billion shopping-search fine in 2024, according to [Engadget](https://www.engadget.com/2206550/google-loses-final-appeal-over-eu-antitrust-fine/).

The company currently faces investigations under the EU's Digital Markets Act over alleged favoritism of its search services and Play Store payment restrictions, according to [Engadget](https://www.engadget.com/2206550/google-loses-final-appeal-over-eu-antitrust-fine/).

## What We Don't Know

The judgment closes this particular case, but its practical effect is limited by the fact that Google says it changed the underlying Android agreements years ago, according to [BleepingComputer](https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/legal/google-loses-final-appeal-to-overturn-41-billion-eu-fine/). The outcome of the separate, ongoing Digital Markets Act investigations into Google's search and Play Store practices remains open, according to [Engadget](https://www.engadget.com/2206550/google-loses-final-appeal-over-eu-antitrust-fine/).
